LESSON: ORAL EXPRESSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.7: Oral Expression

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Oral Expression
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How does expressing ideas accurately enhance communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. use appropriate intonation and pace in oral communication
2. apply appropriate vocabulary for specific communicative functions
3. appreciate the role of interactive speaking for effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Oral Expression

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Oral Expression

Teach
• Focus skill: use appropriate intonation and pace in oral communication.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Oral Expression.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Oral Expression
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does expressing ideas accurately enhance communication?
2. Why is vocabulary important?
3. How do you articulate your thoughts clearly when communicating?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
